en.definition: A statement offered in support of the conclusion of an argument. An argument can have one or many premises.
A claim plus at least one reason offered to support it - the claim is the conclusion and the reasons are the premises. In critical thinking this is not a quarrel but a supported case.
The statement that the premises of an argument are offered to support. It is what the argument is trying to get the audience to accept.
A sentence that claims something is or is not the case - something that can, in principle, be true or false.
A conclusion the reader draws from evidence in the text.
A network device that connects machines in one place and forwards each message only to the machine it is addressed to.
The set of mental functions - remembering, imagining, believing, deciding and reasoning - through which a person takes in information and works on it.
A premise the argument depends on but does not state, usually because it seemed obvious to the writer. It is not concealed; it is simply left unsaid.
Who the text is written for.
A rule that repeats or grows, such as a matchstick pattern that adds 2 sticks for every new triangle.

en.definition: A question that admits more than one reasonable answer and requires reasoning rather than retrieval to settle. An argument is needed.
A question that has a single verifiable answer established by looking, counting, measuring or checking a record. No argument is needed to settle it.
A shape with three sides whose angles sum to 180 degrees; its area is half the enclosing rectangle with the same base and height.
A model of communication with three corners: speaker, audience and subject. The same message takes a different shape depending on which corner moves.
Who the text is written for.
A question that invites more than one reasonable answer - something people can disagree about and that needs reasoning rather than a single factual lookup.
A claim plus at least one reason offered to support it - the claim is the conclusion and the reasons are the premises. In critical thinking this is not a quarrel but a supported case.
The statement that the premises of an argument are offered to support. It is what the argument is trying to get the audience to accept.
A statement offered in support of the conclusion of an argument. An argument can have one or many premises.
A named collection of data stored by the operating system, identified by its name and extension, its folder path, and its metadata.

وہ بیان جس کی طرف دلائل دیے جاتے ہیں۔ یہ وہ بات ہے جس کا ارگ نے سننے والے کمنے قبول کرنے کی کوشش کی ہے۔
